question: Despite the protection of the feral urban pigeon under the Birds Directive1, as clarified in the Commission’s guidance document on the general system of protection of bird species of 31 March 2026, many French cities continue to use lethal methods involving considerable suffering to manage their pigeon populations.

Epidemiological studies show objectively that pigeons do not pose a threat to public health, as the risk of pigeons transmitting diseases to humans is negligible. Therefore, there is no reason to grant derogations under Article 9 of the directive to municipalities that seek to get rid of pigeons year after year by cruel means, such as capturing and killing them. In this context: 1.
How many derogations for the capture and killing of urban pigeons have been issued by the Member States, particularly France, and what was the reason for this?

What action does the Commission intend to take against Member States, particularly France, when cities that do not have a derogation use methods prohibited by Article 5 of the Birds Directive, such as the capture and killing of urban pigeons?
Directive 2009/147/EC of 30 November 2009 on the conservation of wild birds (ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2009/147/oj). 1
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.11.2026) Statistics on derogations reported by Member States under the Birds Directive1, including those concerning the Rock Pigeon (Columba livia) are available on the European Environment Agency dashboard2. The dashboard provides information on reported derogations, including species concerned, the activities authorised and the legal justifications.

These statistics provide an overview of the number of derogations reported for the species and the purpose for which they were granted. The Birds Directive establishes a general system of protection for all naturally occurring wild bird species in the European territory of Member States to which the Treaties apply.

Article 5 requires the establishment of a protection system for bird species, listing particular prohibitions. Article 9 ensures that the system of protection is balanced against other important interests by defining circumstances where the use of derogations is possible.

Without prejudice to the Commission’s role as guardian of the Treaties, Member States are primarily responsible for ensuring compliance with EU law. This includes verifying whether any derogations granted by local authorities, such as cities, is compliant with the conditions laid down in Article 9.

The Commission published dedicated guidance to support Member States in the application of the provisions of Articles 5 and 9 of the Directive3. As regards the specific situation referred to, the Commission does not systematically investigate individual local cases, unless they point to a broader failure by a Member State to correctly apply and enforce EU law4.
1 Directive 2009/147/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 30 November 2009 on the

conservation of wild birds, OJ L 20, 26.1.2010, p. 7–25. 2 https://www.eea.europa.eu/en/analysis/maps-and-charts/overview-of-derogations-and-exceptions-dashboards. 3 Commission Notice – Guidance document on the general system of protection of bird species – Article 5 and Article 9 of the Birds Directive, C/2026/4988, OJ C, C/2026/4094, 31.7.

4 As set out in the Communication of 19 January 2017 (EU law: Better results through better application C/2016/8600, OJ C 18, 19.1.2017, p. 10–20) and in the Communication of 13 October 2022 COM(2022) 518 final - Enforcing EU law for a Europe that delivers.
